descriptionChirho: To seize, capture, or take hold of a person, city, or object by force (Qal active forms including perfects, imperfects, imperatives, consecutive imperfects, conjunctive perfects, infinitives with prepositions, and infinitive absolute).

To handle, wield, or play a tool, weapon, or musical instrument, indicating skillful use rather than forceful seizure (Qal participle forms with Arabic عَازِف 'player' and Korean 다루는 'handling' confirming distinct sense).
To be overlaid or covered with a material such as metal (Qal passive participle with unique meaning confirmed by Arabic مُغَشّى 'covered' and Korean 입혀졌으나 'coated').
To be seized, caught, or captured, expressing the passive of forceful taking (Nifal forms including perfects, imperfects, consecutive imperfects, and infinitive).
To seize or grasp firmly with intensified or sustained action (Piel stem indicating intensive aspect, confirmed by Arabic تَتَمَسَّكُ form V reflexive-intensive 'hold fast').
